speaker_role: independent educational consultant (Nick, Daw Academic Consulting)
commercial_incentive: yes - offers a free consultation booking link in the video description
key_insights: The first and overriding rule after a deferral is to follow each college's specific stated directions exactly and not submit unsolicited extra materials
Most colleges deferring an applicant will still require a mid-year report (updated first-semester grades) to bring the application up to par with regular-decision applicants
If a school counselor sends a mass email confirming they will handle mid-year reports automatically, students should not personally follow up and add to counselor workload

Updated test scores (e.g., a November SAT taken too late for the early round) can often still be sent to regular-decision schools if allowed; students should call or email to confirm rather than guess
A letter of continued interest (LOCI) is a half-to-one-page update on developments since applying, meant to reaffirm fit and bring the application current with three extra months of achievements

For sending a LOCI, address it to the person who signed the deferral letter if it appears to be an admissions officer/regional rep (not a dean/administrator), or to the general admissions office if unclear
If a school explicitly says it does not want letters of continued interest, do not send one regardless of how compelling the update
specific_numbers_or_facts: Regular decision results are described as arriving anywhere from January 3 to February, or as late as March/April for rolling-admission schools, per the speaker
notable_or_distinctive: Provides an unusually concrete decision tree for figuring out who to address a letter of continued interest to, based on who signed the original deferral letter.
reliability_notes: General consultant advice presented confidently but without institutional citations; some claims (e.g., typical mid-year report timing, LOCI norms) are generalized practices that can vary significantly by individual college.
